It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: For this cluster_troubleshooting case, state the verified node/GPU/NIC topology and affinity, PCIe/NVLink paths, software and firmware versions, MTU, transport, registration permissions, GPU-direct capability, workload and message-size distribution, concurrency, clocks, and unknowns. Trace a representative operation from the framework through the communication library, verbs work requests and completions, registered host or GPU memory, queue pairs, NIC/link, and peer endpoint. RDMA may reduce host copies and CPU involvement, but GPU-direct, transport selection, and fallback must be measured rather than assumed. Define a falsifiable hypothesis: on a fixed workload the verified RDMA path reduces p50 or p95 communication time by at least 10-15% versus an interleaved matched non-RDMA baseline, without worsening p99 step time, CPU saturation, retries, timeouts, error rate, or correctness. Measure end-to-end step time separately from communication and overlap time, throughput, CPU, bandwidth, p50/p95/p99, completion latency, queue occupancy, retries, timeouts, link errors, and relevant NIC/GPU counters with explicit units and synchronized timestamps. Exclude warm-up, randomize repeated trials, control topology, clocks, message sizes, batching, and competing load, and report distributions, uncertainty, and confounders. Diagnose capability/registration, completions and queue pressure, congestion, physical link health, and fallback in that order; correlate device counters with application traces. Bound retries and recovery, verify outputs, and roll back to the last known-good path when a predeclared tail-latency, error, or correctness threshold is breached. Test link failure only in an isolated environment. Missing platform facts or telemetry are evidence gaps, not facts to invent.
